sources.population: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics (DHC), Table P1, by ZCTA
sources.boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_zcta520_500k

splitline.label: Shortest splitline
splitline.desc: Cut the state with the shortest straight line that divides its population in the right ratio (e.g. 9 seats → 4:5), then cut each half the same way until every piece is one district. No settings, so only one possible map.

splitcounty.label: Splitline + counties
splitcounty.desc: Shortest splitline, but the pieces being cut are whole counties: at each cut, counties go to the side their population center falls on, and only the one county where the population ratio is reached is divided, along the straight line. Borders then settle on county lines where they can.

county.label: Counties first
county.desc: Like Iowa's nonpartisan process: districts take whole counties wherever population allows and split a county only when they must. Growth starts in the northwest; borders prefer county lines.

center.label: State center
center.desc: Each state fills outward from the middle of its map extent. District 1 surrounds the central ZIP; later districts form around it.

nw.label: NW corner
nw.desc: Each state fills from its northwest corner. District 1 grows from the ZIP nearest that corner; each new district starts at the unassigned ZIP closest to it.

ne.label: NE corner
ne.desc: Each state fills from its northeast corner. District 1 grows from the ZIP nearest that corner; each new district starts at the unassigned ZIP closest to it.

zip.label: ZIP number
zip.desc: Each state starts at its lowest-numbered ZIP, and a growing district always adds the neighboring ZIP with the lowest number. Postal numbering follows mail-sorting regions, so districts follow them too.

best.label: Best score
best.desc: For each state, take every other mode's map and keep the one with the smoothest borders (fewest split neighbor links), among maps within ±2% of ideal. The rule was fixed before any map was drawn.

random.label: Random draw
random.desc: One random map per state, built by cutting random spanning trees. The random seed comes from a public number published before the maps (the 2020 apportionment total), so anyone can rerun it and get the same map. No rerolls.
